questions.question: The Synonym of the word "benevolence" is :-
questions.questionHtml: The Synonym of the word "benevolence" is :-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (1) i.e. "Compassion".

Key Points

  • 'Benevolence': (उदारता) - The quality of being well-meaning and kind.
    • Example: Her benevolence was evident when she donated her inheritance to charity.
  • Compassion: (दया) - Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
    • Example: The nurse showed great compassion towards her patients.
  • Benevolence relates to kindness and a desire to do good, closely associated with compassion's focus on sympathy and concern.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Compassion".

Additional Information

  • Callousness: (कठोरता) - Insensitivity and cruelty towards others.
  • Hard-hearted: (कठोर हृदय) - Unfeeling; not easily moved by emotions.
  • Beneficial: (लाभकारी) - Resulting in good; favorable or advantageous.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. HYDRIC
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

HYDRIC
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Xeric.

Key Points

  • The word "Hydric" refers to something related to water or requiring a significant amount of moisture. (पानी से संबंधित)
    • Example: Wetlands are considered hydric environments as they are saturated with water for most of the year.
  • "Xeric" is the antonym of hydric and refers to an environment or condition that is extremely dry or requires minimal water. (अत्यधिक शुष्क)
    • Example: Cacti are xeric plants that thrive in desert-like conditions with very little water.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Hydric' is 'Xeric'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (Xeric).

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Mesic (आर्द्र): Refers to environments that are moderately moist, neither too wet nor too dry.
    • Example: A mesic forest typically has balanced rainfall and supports diverse plant species.
  • Aquiferous (जलवाही): Refers to something that carries or contains water.
    • Example: Aquiferous rocks are crucial for storing and supplying groundwater.
  • Succulent (रसदार): Refers to plants or parts of plants that are juicy or have thick, fleshy tissues for storing water.
    • Example: Aloe vera is a succulent plant known for its medicinal properties.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a logical passage: A. This shift altered traditional communication patterns. B. Social media platforms gained rapid popularity. C. People began sharing opinions instantly. D. As a result, information spread faster than ever before.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a logical passage:

A. This shift altered traditional communication patterns.

B. Social media platforms gained rapid popularity.

C. People began sharing opinions instantly.

D. As a result, information spread faster than ever before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The paragraph begins with Sentence B, which introduces the rapid popularity of social media platforms.
  • Sentence C follows as it explains the instant sharing of opinions due to social media:
    • "People began sharing opinions instantly."
  • Sentence A comes next as it describes the shift in traditional communication patterns:
    • "This shift altered traditional communication patterns."
  • Sentence D is the last, highlighting the result of faster information spread:
    • "As a result, information spread faster than ever before."
  • The correct sequence is B C A D.
 
Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:
"Social media platforms gained rapid popularity. People began sharing opinions instantly. This shift altered traditional communication patterns. As a result, information spread faster than ever before."

questions.question: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Hitesh said, "Bharat will take care of the cats while we are away."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Hitesh said, "Bharat will take care of the cats while we are away."

options.text: Hitesh said that Bharat should take care of the cats while we are away.
options.html: Hitesh said that Bharat should take care of the cats while we are away.

options.text: Hitesh said that Bharat had to take care of the cats while they were away.
options.html: Hitesh said that Bharat had to take care of the cats while they were away.

options.text: Hitesh said that Bharat will take care of the cats while they are away.
options.html: Hitesh said that Bharat will take care of the cats while they are away.

options.text: Hitesh said that Bharat would take care of the cats while they were away.
options.html: Hitesh said that Bharat would take care of the cats while they were away.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Hitesh said that Bharat would take care of the cats while they were away.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the given question we have to change it into Indirect Speech.
  • The process of transformation is as follows:
    • Comma and inverted commas will be removed.
    • The conjunction 'that' will be added.
    • The helping verb is changed according to the tense, followed by the 3rd form of the verb. (will changes into would)
    • The present simple tense i.e. are away will be changed to the past simple tense i.e. were away.
    • The pronoun 'we' will be changed into 'they' because the first person pronouns are changed according to the subject of the reporting verb.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: Hitesh said that Bharat would take care of the cats while they were away.

Additional Information

  • The fllowing table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:
Direct Speech Indirect Speech
Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

questions.question: Fill in the blank using the correct option.In case no article is needed, select option No Article. I went and informed ______ police about the theft.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank using the correct option.In case no article is needed, select option No Article.

I went and informed ______ police about the theft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'the'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence is referring to a specific group of people, namely the police.
  • We are not talking about any police officer in particular, but rather the police force as a whole.
  • Hence, 'the' is the correct article to use.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
Complete Sentence: I went and informed the police about the theft.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: a is incorrect because it is used to refer to a single, unspecified member of a group. In this case, we are not talking about a single police officer, but rather the entire police force.
  • Option 2: an is incorrect for the same reason as option 1.
  • Option 4: No Article is incorrect because the sentence is referring to a specific group of people, namely the police. Therefore, an article is needed.

questions.question: A sentence is given in the Direct/Indirect form. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in the Indirect/Direct form: "Please open my bag and check if my Physics note­book is there" Rakesh said to Rajesh.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is given in the Direct/Indirect form. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in the Indirect/Direct form:

"Please open my bag and check if my Physics note­book is there" Rakesh said to Rajesh.

options.text: Rakesh requested Rajesh to open his bag and check if his Physics note­book was there.
options.html: Rakesh requested Rajesh to open his bag and check if his Physics note­book was there.

options.text: Rakesh requested Rajesh to open his bag and see if his Physics note­book is there.
options.html: Rakesh requested Rajesh to open his bag and see if his Physics note­book is there.

options.text: Rakesh asked Rajesh to open his bag and check if his Physics note­book is there.
options.html: Rakesh asked Rajesh to open his bag and check if his Physics note­book is there.

options.text: Rakesh ordered Rajesh to open his bag and see if his Physics note­book was there.
options.html: Rakesh ordered Rajesh to open his bag and see if his Physics note­book was there.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. ​Rakesh requested Rajesh to open his bag and check if his Physics note­book was there.

 

  • Here the given sentence is in direct speech and it is an imperative sentence as marked by the use of ‘please’
  • In imperative sentences, 'said to' is changed to 'ordered, requested, suggested, commanded, forbade, warned, etc.' as per the context of the sentence.
  • The conjunction 'to' is used after the reported verb in imperative sentences.
  • After 'to', the first form of the verb is used,i.e. V1.  So, write 'to open'.
  • The pronoun in reported speech is changed according to the subject and object of reporting part of the direct speech. So, 'my' will change according to 'Rakesh'. hence, write 'his' in reported speech (Indirect speech)

 

 Explanation

  • As the given sentence is marked by the use of 'please'  So ‘requested’ will be used as a reporting verb in Indirect speech
  • Requested is given in option 1 and 2 only; thus, option 3 and 4 can be eliminated easily
  • In imperative sentences, we generally don't change the tense of the verb in the reported speech. We use a 'to-infinitive' and retain the base form of the verb (V1); here we are not changing to + v1 form of the verb, but is there will change into 'was there'
  • Hence according to the rules, it concludes that Option 1 is the correct answer

 

Correct Sentence-Rakesh requested Rajesh to open his bag and check if his Physics note­book was there.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the right order to form a meaningful sentence. A. a survey on parking in Delhi B. in the city were under-utilised C. found that several multi-level car parks D. because there was no parking charge on public land
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the right order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. a survey on parking in Delhi

B. in the city were under-utilised

C. found that several multi-level car parks

D. because there was no parking charge on public land
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
Key Points
  • The sentence fragments need to be arranged in a logical order to form a meaningful sentence.
  • Sentence A is the first part, as it introduces the subject of the survey:
    • "A survey on parking in Delhi."
  • Sentence C follows, as it reveals the findings of the survey:
    • "found that several multi-level car parks."
  • Sentence B is the next logical part, as it explains the under-utilisation of the car parks:
    • "in the city were under-utilised."
  • Sentence D concludes the sentence by providing the reason for the under-utilisation:
    • "because there was no parking charge on public land."
  • The correct sequence is ACBD.
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"A survey on parking in Delhi found that several multi-level car parks in the city were under-utilised because there was no parking charge on public land."

questions.question: The following question consists of an incomplete sentence. The missing part of the sentence has been split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and labelled P, Q, R, S. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence. The transition toward a green hydrogen economy is often touted as the definitive solution to the intermittency of renewable energy _______________________________________________ while simultaneously reshaping the traditional hierarchies of global energy diplomacy. P. by leveraging surplus electrolytic capacity to decouple power generation from immediate demand Q. although this transition necessitates a massive overhaul of existing cryogenic infrastructure R. and requiring a level of international regulatory synchronization seldom seen in industrial history S. effectively transforming volatile wind and solar inputs into a stable, transportable chemical commodity
questions.questionHtml:
The following question consists of an incomplete sentence. The missing part of the sentence has been split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and labelled P, Q, R, S. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

The transition toward a green hydrogen economy is often touted as the definitive solution to the intermittency of renewable energy _______________________________________________ while simultaneously reshaping the traditional hierarchies of global energy diplomacy.

P. by leveraging surplus electrolytic capacity to decouple power generation from immediate demand
Q. although this transition necessitates a massive overhaul of existing cryogenic infrastructure
R. and requiring a level of international regulatory synchronization seldom seen in industrial history
S. effectively transforming volatile wind and solar inputs into a stable, transportable chemical commodity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence introduces the transition toward a green hydrogen economy as the solution to renewable energy intermittency.
  • Part P starts the sentence as it explains leveraging surplus electrolytic capacity to decouple power generation from demand:
    • "By leveraging surplus electrolytic capacity to decouple power generation from immediate demand."
  • Part S follows as it explains how this process transforms renewable inputs into a stable commodity:
    • "Effectively transforming volatile wind and solar inputs into a stable, transportable chemical commodity."
  • Part Q is next as it introduces the necessary overhaul of cryogenic infrastructure:
    • "Although this transition necessitates a massive overhaul of existing cryogenic infrastructure."
  • Part R concludes the sentence by highlighting the requirement for international regulatory synchronization:
    • "And requiring a level of international regulatory synchronization seldom seen in industrial history."
  • The correct sequence is P – S – Q – R.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"The transition toward a green hydrogen economy is often touted as the definitive solution to the intermittency of renewable energy by leveraging surplus electrolytic capacity to decouple power generation from immediate demand, effectively transforming volatile wind and solar inputs into a stable, transportable chemical commodity, although this transition necessitates a massive overhaul of existing cryogenic infrastructure and requiring a level of international regulatory synchronization seldom seen in industrial history."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to complete the given proverb. As you sow, So ______ you reap.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given proverb.

As you sow, So ______ you reap.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Shall'.

Key Points

  • Here, the proverb 'As you sow, So shall you reap'.
  • It means future consequences are inevitably shaped by present actions.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A couple of parrots ________ on the telephone wires.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Out of the four alternatives, choose the one which can be substituted for the given words/sentences. A state of being pleasantly lost in one's dreams
questions.questionHtml:
Out of the four alternatives, choose the one which can be substituted for the given words/sentences.

A state of being pleasantly lost in one's dreams
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Reverie".

Key Points

  • Reverie means a state of being pleasantly lost in one's thoughts; a daydream. This exactly matches the provided definition.
    • For example, "On sunny afternoons, he often sat on the park bench, lost in a peaceful reverie."
  • Hence, the correct answer will be Option 3.

Additional Information

  • Option 1: Hallucination refers to an experience involving the apparent perception of something not present, typically as a result of a mental disorder or of taking drugs. This does not fit the given definition as it implies a distortion of reality rather than a pleasant daydream.
  • Option 2: Fantasy usually refers to the faculty or activity of imagining impossible or improbable things, and while this may involve daydreaming, it does not necessarily imply being pleasantly lost in one's thoughts.
  • Option 4: Illusion refers to a deceptive appearance or impression, or a false idea or belief, which does not fit the given definition.
  • Therefore, after evaluating all options, reverie (Option 3) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Direction : Choose the correct sentence from the following:
questions.questionHtml: Direction: Choose the correct sentence from the following:

options.text: She can have neither tea not coffee.
options.html: She can have neither tea not coffee.

options.text: He neither keeps the keys himself not leaves them with his wife.
options.html: He neither keeps the keys himself not leaves them with his wife.

options.text: He was wearing neither a shirt nor a coat.
options.html: He was wearing neither a shirt nor a coat.

options.text: Neither he not his wife may attend the function.
options.html: Neither he not his wife may attend the function.

questions.solution:
The correct answer- 'He was wearing neither a shirt nor a coat.'

Key Points

  • The sentences 'She can have neither tea not coffee.', 'He neither keeps the keys himself not leaves them with his wife.' and 'Neither he not his wife may attend the function.' are incorrect.
    • We can use neither as a conjunction with nor.
    • It connects two or more negative alternatives. 
      • Example: Neither Brian nor his wife mentioned anything about moving house.
    • ​Therefore, 'not' should be replaced with 'nor' to make the sentences grammatically correct.
       

Thus, the correct sentence is 'He was wearing neither a shirt nor a coat.'

Additional Information

  • Conjunctions are words that link other words, phrases, or clauses together.
  • Conjunctions allow you to form complex, elegant sentences and avoid the choppiness of multiple short sentences.
    • Example: I like cooking and eating, but I don’t like washing dishes afterwards. 

​​

  • वाक्य 'She can have neither tea not coffee.', 'He neither keeps the keys himself not leaves them with his wife.' और 'Neither he not his wife may attend the function.' गलत हैं।
    • हम neither का उपयोग संयोजन के रूप में nor के साथ कर सकते हैं।
    • यह दो या अधिक नकारात्मक विकल्पों को जोड़ता है।
      • उदाहरण: Neither Brian nor his wife mentioned anything about moving house.​​
    • इसलिए, वाक्यों को व्याकरणिक रूप से सही बनाने के लिए 'not' का उपयोग 'nor' के साथ प्रतिस्थापित किया जाना चाहिए।

questions.question: Choose the word which expresses nearly the opposite meaning of the given word " SUSPICION ".
questions.questionHtml: Choose the word which expresses nearly the opposite meaning of the given word " SUSPICION ".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Belief'. (संदेह)

    • Example: She had a suspicion that her husband was cheating on her.
  • Belief: the feeling of being certain that something exists or true 
    • Example: He has firm belief in God.

questions.question: Some phrases are given below together with their meanings. Choose the correct meaning of the phrase. To die in harness
questions.questionHtml:
Some phrases are given below together with their meanings. Choose the correct meaning of the phrase.

To die in harness
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The phrase "To die in harness" means to die while still working or actively engaged in one's responsibilities. (काम करते हुए मरना)
    • Example: Despite his illness, he continued to work tirelessly and eventually died in harness.
  • "Die in harness" implies dedication and commitment to work until the end of one's life. (हठ या जिम्मेदारी में अंत तक काम करते रहना)
    • Example: The old professor passed away while teaching his last class—he truly died in harness.
  • Hence, we can conclude that the correct meaning of "To die in harness" is "to die while still working."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: To die on horseback (घोड़े पर मरना): Refers to literally dying while riding a horse.
    • Example: The warrior fell during the battle and died on horseback.
  • Option 2: To die in the battlefield (युद्धभूमि में मरना): Refers to dying while fighting in a war or battle.
    • Example: He was a brave soldier who died in the battlefield defending his country.
  • Option 4: To die with honour (सम्मान के साथ मरना): Refers to dying in a way that earns respect or recognition.
    • Example: The soldier died with honour during his last mission.
  • Option 5: No valid meaning for this option is provided in the context of the phrase. (कोई मान्य अर्थ नहीं)

questions.question: Which tense and form fits best? (1)
questions.questionHtml: Which tense and form fits best? (1)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'encapsulates'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence describes a general fact or a characteristic of sushi within Japanese culture, which requires the Present Simple tense.
